newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Uzbeks aim for 4 mln T grain harvest in 97 -agency.
newsitem.headline: Uzbeks aim for 4 mln T grain harvest in 97 -agency.

text.p: Uzbekistan aims to produce 4.0 million tonnes of grain in 1997, up from 2.7 million in 1996, Russia's Interfax news agency said on Monday.
Zair Latypov, a senior official at the Agriculture Ministry, was quoted as saying that the condition of the winter crop "makes for a fully realistic prediction of four million tonnes of grain".
Latypov said 2.5 million hectares had been sown to grains, with 1.0 million of the total under irrigation.

Uzbekistan's President Islam Karimov wants the former Soviet republic to become self-sufficient. Officials estimate annual needs at 4.0-4.5 million tonnes of grain for the 23 million-strong population.
Last year's harvest was well below Uzbekistan's ambitious, Soviet-style production target of 4.5 million tonnes.
Uzbek grain sources said in February that the country would need to import 1.0-1.2 million tonnes of food wheat this year, adding that the country imported around 1.6 million in 1996.
